title: D-dimer
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It helps show whether there are fresh blood clots in your blood vessels.
why: For a possible clot in the leg or lungs, sometimes in pregnancy, after surgery, or with some illnesses.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the same or the next day
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or recently gave birth
If you recently had surgery or an injury
If one leg is swollen and painful

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually nothing special. Best fasting or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 day. The lab will tell you when
A high D-dimer is not a diagnosis. The doctor may order a vein ultrasound or other tests
red_flags: Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood: call emergency services. Do not wait for the test
One leg suddenly swells, turns red, and hurts: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: Does a high D-dimer mean I have a clot?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It goes up in pregnancy, with inflammation, after surgery, and with age. Your doctor decides.

faq.q: Why do this test if I feel fine?
faq.a: Sometimes it is ordered for monitoring, for example in pregnancy. Ask your doctor why.

reminders.text: D-dimer test tomorrow. Best to come before eating. Water is fine.
